Hi Alex — thanks for the quick report and the trace. Sorry for the interruption. We’re investigating immediately.

Quick notes / immediate mitigations you can try while we triage:
- Temporarily switch to the non-streaming (batch) generation endpoint for the most critical flows — this avoids client-side partial renders and eliminates stream pacing dependence.
- If you must keep streaming, try reducing max_tokens to 128 and lower the chunk size on your client (if configurable) so fewer tokens are held before emission.
- Enable client-side exponential backoff on stalled streams and a short reconnect window (2–3s) — we’ve seen this help user experience when tokens arrive irregularly.
- Share any additional session IDs; we’ve requested more telemetry from the edge.

I’ve attached a quick client replay guide that describes how to capture a minimal reproducer. We’ll revert with findings and a timeline by EOD.

Hi Alex / team — quick update from engineering after the initial triage. TL;DR: a recent routing policy tweak caused an uneven distribution of streaming requests across our us-west edge fleet, which increased per-connection queueing and caused token pacing irregularities for a subset of long-running streaming sessions. We rolled back that routing change at 01:10 UTC and deployed a hotfix to reduce KV cache thrash for streaming sessions; both mitigations are active.

Root cause (short):
- A policy that favored lower-cost hosts was introduced during a capacity optimization deploy at ~09:55 PDT. For certain chat traffic patterns (long-lived streaming sessions with intermittent token emission), that routing increased head-of-line blocking in a few edge nodes.
- The edge queueing caused the backend token emission to be delayed in bursts (3–8s) for affected connections.

What we did (already):
- Rolled back the routing policy to the previous distribution at 01:10 UTC.
- Applied a hotfix to the streaming pipeline to favor active KV entries for open sessions, which reduces cache churn.
- Added short-term telemetry to capture per-connection enqueue times and early-drop reasons.

Customer-facing mitigations you can apply now (recommendation order):
1) Pin calls to the verified variant redwood-llama-13b-v1f (this variant is on the more consistent streaming path right now).
2) For critical flows, switch to non-streaming endpoint until we confirm steady state across edges (we expect stabilization in ~6–12 hours).
3) Lower max_tokens to 128 and avoid very long-lived single-stream sessions; use partial conversations with explicit continuation if you need >128 tokens.
4) Enable a client-side 2–3s jittered reconnect if streams stall — this hides brief bursts while we fully normalize routing.

Timeline & next steps:
- We see measurable reduction in token pauses since the rollback. We’re monitoring closely and will post a full postmortem with root cause analysis and permanent remediation items within 72 hours.
- We’ll reach out to customers individually with any suggested configuration changes and can assist with pinning variants or testing.

Attachments: [postmortem-draft.md] (internal, draft)

Apologies for the disruption — we know streaming UX is core to your product. I or Irene can set up a short call to walk through the steps and help apply the temporary mitigations.

—Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
